classification.difficultyReason: Complete complementary colour distributions, allocate a missing remainder in a two-to-one ratio and explain the event equivalence.

content.prompt: A bag contains blue, green, and red counters.

inlines.text: Green is twice as likely to be picked as blue.

answer.worked: The Blue entry in the table gives $P(\text{blue})=19\%$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{not green nor red})&=1-P(\text{green or red})\\P(\text{not green nor red})&=100\%-81\%\\P(\text{not green nor red})&=19\%\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Not green nor red is the same as blue.
answer.worked: The bag contains only green, red and blue counters. The complement of green or red is blue, so both probabilities are $19\%$.
